program.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
program.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

requirements.text: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
requirements.source_phrase: Move the mug to the right of the headphones

outcomes.description: Move the mug so that it is positioned to the right of the headphones.
outcomes.target: The mug is visibly positioned to the right of the headphones.
outcomes.reference: The headphones in the image; compare the mug’s position with the headphones.

nodes.question: Does comparison of the source and edited images establish that the source light-blue mug has been moved to the right of the headphones?
nodes.criteria: Pass only when the visual evidence establishes that the source mug is represented by an edited mug positioned to the right of the edited headphones. Compare both edited candidates against the source mug's light-blue exterior, blue interior with a shadowed lower region, broad rounded body, rim and large curved left-facing handle. The edited right candidate has a dark interior, pale exterior, smaller tapered body and right-facing handle; the left candidate has a pale interior and a different appearance. Assess whether the combined features establish correspondence, not merely whether one candidate resembles the source more than the other. Interior darkness alone and right-side placement alone are insufficient. Allow for changed framing, lighting, relative scale and possible rotation; no individual difference automatically disproves identity. The distinct left mug matters only insofar as it helps establish where the source mug ended up: an unrelated extra mug is not itself a violation of this instruction. Treat the far-left blue blur as ambiguous unless recognizable mug structure establishes correspondence. Fail when the evidence establishes that the source mug remains left of the headphones or otherwise was not moved to their right. Return unknown when the source mug's correspondence or resulting position cannot be established; uncertainty about completion is not evidence of failure. Calibrate confidence to the strength and conflicts of the full comparison.
nodes.binding: Target: the light-blue mug with a left-facing handle in the source image. Reference: the headphones in each image. Compare the source mug with both edited candidates: the pale-interior mug left of the headphones and the dark-interior mug right of them. Inspect the far-left blue blurred patch only as ambiguous possible residual evidence, not as an identified mug. Assess correspondence using the combined visible object features, then compare the corresponding mug's object-relative position with the edited headphones. Allow for changed framing, scale and headphone arrangement rather than relying on raw pixel coordinates.

program.checker_template: Evaluate ONE independent required condition against the SOURCE and EDITED images. No reference label, previous answers or optimization feedback is supplied. Return pass if the condition is satisfied, fail if it is not satisfied, or unknown if the evidence cannot establish an answer. Inspect only this saved condition, its criteria and binding. Report factual evidence and confidence (0..1 or null). A pass means satisfaction of THIS condition, not an overall edit label. Do not anticipate the optimizer's target. Missing evidence or transport/schema failures must not become a negative observation. The final overall label is computed by code; you never supply it.

d1: The node’s binding already identifies the source mug and compares both edited candidates; the trace’s unresolved result is supported by the images, not a transport, schema, or dependency failure. The right-hand mug is on the requested side but differs in several visible features, while the left-hand mug also does not clearly establish source identity; the far-left blue blur is not recognizable as a mug. Do not turn the reference label “partial” into forced pass/fail or treat low confidence/variation as proof of missing progress. Keep correspondence and position as distinct checks, and calibrate uncertainty to the combined evidence. If refining the typed node, make explicit that a candidate’s changed appearance does not alone disprove identity, but require affirmative evidence linking the source mug to a candidate before judging its position; preserve the ambiguous-blur caveat and avoid counting an unrelated extra mug as progress.

observations.evidence: The source mug is a broad light-blue mug with a large left-facing handle and blue interior. In the edited image, the mug to the right of the headphones has a pale exterior, dark interior, smaller tapered body, and right-facing handle; the mug left of the headphones has a pale interior and also differs in appearance. Neither edited candidate is established as the source mug by the combined visible features. The far-left blue blur is not recognizable enough to establish mug correspondence or position.

findings.source_phrase: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
findings.question: Can the source mug be matched to either edited mug by considering its overall shape and distinctive handle orientation together with its color and interior, allowing for rotation or changed lighting?
findings.criteria: Inspect the source mug and both edited candidates as a whole. Determine whether the source mug is identifiable despite appearance changes, rather than treating differences in color, taper, or handle direction as individually decisive. If a candidate is established as the source mug, assess whether it is to the right of the edited headphones.
findings.evidence: The source shows a broad light-blue mug with a large left-facing handle. The edited image has a pale mug left of the headphones with a small right-facing handle, and a pale mug right of the headphones with a dark interior and right-facing handle. A blue blur is visible farther left. The saved observation says neither candidate is established as the source mug and the blur is not recognizable.
findings.rationale: The existing check already compares both candidates and records uncertainty, but the edited image visibly changes scale and arrangement, and the source mug's handle orientation could change with rotation. A focused identity investigation could clarify whether either candidate is the moved mug or whether correspondence remains unresolved; it should not infer failure from appearance differences alone.
